pattern.short_summary: A finished artifact that the system did not produce is decomposed back into an underlying structure — data table, encoding spec, component graph, layered representation — and that recovered structure becomes the object the user manipulates.
pattern.definition: A finished artifact that the system did not produce is decomposed back into an underlying structure — data table, encoding spec, component graph, layered representation — and that recovered structure becomes the object the user manipulates. The original rendered form is treated as output whose source has been lost and must be reconstructed. Editing happens on the recovered structure, not on the surface.
pattern.structural_signature: An ingestion step takes a rendered or compiled artifact and emits a structured representation of it (typed nodes, fields, layers, specs); that representation is bound to the editing surface, and changes to it re-render the artifact. The recovery is inverse to the artifact's own production pipeline, and the representation is richer than the surface it was derived from.

dimension.category_description: How users inspect, modify, scope, revise, accept, program, or interrupt generated work at the artifact level.
dimension.classification_boundary: Centers user control during or after generation, including editable intermediate generators and representations.
